label: prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix
title: Beta decay as a universal matrix-valued polynomial in $q$
html:
Proposition. Beta decay as a universal matrix-valued polynomial in q

Beta decay is mediated by the T_{3,5} torus knot with 10 crossings. The T_{3,5} insertion at the converting quark produces a universal 2\times2 matrix-valued polynomial \Delta_\beta(q) that governs every beta transition in every nucleus. The transfer matrix captures the effect of the 10-crossing weak vertex on each nucleon pair.

The three crossing transfer matrices

Each nucleon pair (i, j) contributes a transfer matrix T(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]):

  T(c, d) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\
    c & d
  \end{pmatrix}

with crossing coefficients (c, d) depending on the pair type. The (1, -(q - q^{-1})) convention for nn crossings is the unique convention consistent with the Hecke inverse relation \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - (q - q^{-1}):

  T_{pp}(q) =  T(1, 0) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  T_{nn}(q) =  T(1, -(q - q^{-1})) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    0 & 1 \\
    1 & -(q - q^{-1})
  \end{pmatrix}
  T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q) =  T\!\left(1, -\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\right) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) & 1 \\[4pt]
    1 & -\frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
  \end{pmatrix}

All three matrices live in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]) — no fractional powers of q appear. The pp and nn transfer matrices are unimodular: \det T_{pp} = \det T_{nn} = -1 (forced by the Hecke eigenvalues q \cdot (-q^{-1}) = -1). The mixed crossing \frac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}) is an algebraic average, not a group element, so \det T_{\mathrm{mix}} \neq -1.

The universal beta decay matrix

Proposition. The two elementary decay matrices \Delta_\beta^{nn \to \mathrm{mix}} and \Delta_\beta^{\mathrm{mix} \to pp} are identical:

  \Delta_\beta^{nn \to \mathrm{mix}}(q)
  =  T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q) - T_{nn}(q)
  =  T_{pp}(q) - T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q)
  =  \Delta_\beta^{\mathrm{mix} \to pp}(q)

There is a single universal beta decay matrix:

  \boxed{
    \Delta_\beta(q)
    = 
    \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \mathbb{I}
  }

where \mathbb{I} is the 2 \times 2 identity. The decay matrix is a scalar multiple of the identity — beta decay uniformly scales all channels by \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}).
